title: QuFEM: Fast and Accurate Quantum Readout Calibration Using the Finite Element Method
problem: Quantum readout noise is the most significant source of error in quantum systems, severely degrading measurement fidelity. Existing matrix-based calibration methods are limited in either scalability to larger qubit counts or achieving high calibration accuracy.
motivation: Improving quantum readout fidelity is critical for achieving reliable quantum computation and practical quantum advantage.
method: QuFEM uses a divide-and-conquer approach formulating calibration as tensor products of noise matrices, iteratively characterizing these matrices with calibrated probability distributions to capture qubit interaction locality. The framework proposes a sparse tensor-product engine that exploits sparsity in intermediate values to accelerate computation compared to dense matrix operations, inspired by classical finite element methods.
key_novelty: Using a sparse tensor-product engine inspired by finite element methods to reduce quantum readout calibration complexity by exploiting intermediate value sparsity for orders-of-magnitude acceleration.
contributions: FEM-inspired divide-and-conquer calibration framework using tensor products of noise matrices to capture qubit interaction locality
Sparse tensor-product engine achieving 2500× speedup in 136-qubit calibration versus state-of-the-art methods
Demonstrated 1.2-1.4× fidelity improvement on real quantum hardware
primary_theme: quantum readout calibration and error mitigation
